On examination, he is tachypneic with a respiratory rate of 28 breaths per minute, oxygen saturation is 88% on room air, and he has diffuse wheezes on auscultation.
Arterial blood gas on room air shows:
Chest X-ray shows increased bronchovascular markings and no focal consolidation.
The patient is diagnosed with a COPD exacerbation likely triggered by a respiratory infection.
He is advised to be admitted for management with supplemental oxygen, antibiotics, and systemic corticosteroids.
However, the patient refuses hospital admission, stating he prefers to be at home.
After addressing potential concerns and ensuring the patient understands the risks of refusing treatment, he remains adamant about not being admitted.

Respiratory rate of 28 breaths per minute, heart rate of 110 beats per minute, blood pressure of 150/90 mmHg, temperature of 37.8°C, and oxygen saturation of 88% on room air
On examination, he is alert but in respiratory distress.
Auscultation reveals diffuse expiratory wheezes and decreased breath sounds at the bases

The patient is started on supplemental oxygen, nebulized albuterol, and intravenous corticosteroids.
Despite initial treatment, his respiratory effort remains high, and his oxygen saturation improves only to 92% on 4 L/min of oxygen via nasal cannula.

On examination, the patient is disoriented to time and place but oriented to person.

He expresses a desire to return home and manage his condition with the help of his daughter.

This 70-year-old male with GOLD Stage IV COPD on home oxygen and recurrent hypercapnic respiratory failure, most recently in January 2022 with confusion, is admitted to the hospital for a community-acquired pneumonia.
He is started on appropriate antibiotics and intravenous fluids.
On hospital day 3, he is noted to have improved clinically and is scheduled for transition to oral antibiotics and discharge the following day.
During the night shift, the patient becomes acutely confused and agitated.

The patient is a 71-year-old male with GOLD Stage IV COPD on home oxygen and recurrent exacerbations requiring prior hospitalizations, most recently in July 2022.
He presents with an acute exacerbation requiring hospitalization and is started on systemic corticosteroids and nebulized bronchodilators.
On hospital day 3, he becomes acutely confused and agitated.
His daughter, who has been at his bedside, reports that he has been "not himself" since earlier in the day.
The nurse reports that the patient received his neighbor's medications this morning due to a chart mix-up; the neighbor is treated for heart failure with digoxin, furosemide, and potassium chloride.

encounters.cc: Worsening shortness of breath and confusion

lines: Worsening shortness of breath and confusion
The patient is a 71-year-old male with GOLD Stage IV COPD on home oxygen therapy who presents with confusion and respiratory symptoms.
He has been hospitalized multiple times for respiratory exacerbations, most recently in March 2023 and July 2022.
His daughter reports that he has had a mild cough with yellow sputum for the past week but began acting strangely earlier this morning.
At baseline, he uses oxygen at home and needs to rest after climbing a single flight of stairs.
Today, he became increasingly drowsy and had difficulty speaking in full sentences.
He also appeared flushed and diaphoretic.
- COPD exacerbation with acute hypercapnic respiratory failure without altered mental status (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis due to excess normal saline infusion (diagnosed 2022-07-15)
- Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (GOLD Stage IV, on home oxygen therapy)
- Heart Failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF)

- Metoprolol succinate 50 mg by mouth daily
- Metformin 500 mg by mouth twice daily
- Insulin glargine 24 units subcutaneous at bedtime
- Mother: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, stroke at age 78
Respiratory rate is 20/min, oxygen saturation is 87% on 2 L/min nasal cannula, and heart rate is 112/min
He is disoriented to time and place.
